title: The NASA Logotype: Use of Color
slide_intent: Teach designers to judge the mark against its actual background. A change in background value can change which lettering a viewer can distinguish.
strategic_value: NASA can keep a recognizable mark across one-color and multicolor applications by changing the foreground to suit the ground.
demonstration: Three signatures compare red, black and warm gray on white. A white logotype on black sits below. The lowest specimen is partly obscured in the scan, while the text supplies the medium-value background rule.
practical_value: Use the background-value guidance to choose black, white or an approved color treatment before placing the master.

content_islands.name: Background guidance
content_islands.spec: Introduce the choices for white, very light, dark and medium-value grounds in columns across the top.

content_islands.name: White-ground alternatives
content_islands.spec: Arrange three signatures on white and hold their proportions and alignment steady as the mark changes color.

content_islands.name: Dark and middle-value specimens
content_islands.spec: Place the white-on-black specimen below the three white-ground signatures. Retain the partly obscured lowest specimen as scanned; use the accompanying text to identify the medium-value rule.

reference_purposes.Expression: The visible specimens compare red, black and warm-gray signatures and white marks on dark grounds.
reference_purposes.Application: The text assigns logotype colors to white, very light, very dark and medium-value backgrounds.
reference_purposes.Constraint: It requires white on black, very dark or NASA-red grounds, and prohibits red on medium or dark grounds; red on very light grounds has a four-color-process exception.

ingredient.name: Logotype foreground color
ingredient.role: Keep the logotype distinct from its background while preserving approved color treatments.
ingredient.application: On white, use the illustrated red-and-black, black or warm-gray treatment. On very light backgrounds, use black, except that red is allowed in very light areas of four-color reproduction. Use white on black, very dark or NASA-red grounds. On medium-value grounds, choose black or white, never red.
ingredient.scope: Background cases in the 1976 manual’s section 1.4. These are historical reproduction rules; the page gives no measured accessibility ratio.
